notes: Active ownership is determined only by a successfully created exclusive-scope lock.
Claiming does not change task status.
Tasks were seeded from the Premium Indie Gap Analysis dated 4 October 2026 and current player-feedback defects.
Tasks are role-owned through primary_agent. Agents normally claim only tasks assigned to their own agent number unless Josh explicitly reassigns the work or the queue is updated.
Supporting agents may advise or review but must not independently implement the primary task without a separate non-overlapping queued scope.
Agent 6 — The Warden is a black-box QA/playtest role. It may create QA reports and non-duplicate follow-up tasks, but should not implement specialist feature fixes inside QA tasks.
Warden findings must include reproduction steps/evidence, severity, player impact and the recommended owner agent. Check the existing queue before creating a new task.
Small PR policy: one claimed task/scope per PR; avoid unrelated refactors. Split broad work into follow-up tasks instead of creating giant integration PRs.
Subjective quality policy: agents may report evidence about clarity, pacing, repetition and friction, but Josh is the creative director and final judge of fun/premium feel.
All black-box Warden QA must drive a real browser (Playwright, agent-browser or equivalent). Reading source/DOM alone is not a playtest.

Agent 7 — The Director owns design governance, not specialist implementation. It reviews work against docs/VISION.md, docs/DECISIONS.md and canonical terminology, flags cross-task conflicts, and proposes queue/dependency corrections.
Josh remains final creative director. The Director may protect and interpret established pillars but must not materially change product direction without Josh's approval.
Before a specialist feature PR is treated as merge-ready, The Director should perform a design-coherence review and record any blocking conflict or terminology/tone issue in the PR or queue.
Narrative authoring may proceed ahead of runtime/save integration when it is isolated to story/docs assets. Blocking engine integration must not unnecessarily idle the Storyteller.

Hear rumours gives immediate visible feedback even when no new rumour is available.

tasks.title: Tactical combat depth and enemy behaviour
tasks.goal: Make combat decisions substantially more interesting without turning Lantern Road into a grid tactics game.
acceptance_criteria: Different enemy archetypes pursue visibly different tactical priorities rather than sharing near-identical behaviour.
Party actions create meaningful choices around targeting, defence, tempo, status effects and resource use.
Enemy intent or other readable telegraphing gives players enough information to make informed decisions.
Combat avoids obvious dominant-action loops and unnecessary click repetition.
Existing encounters remain completable and save/load is not broken.
tasks.notes: Mechanist-owned. Preserve Lantern Road's compact card/target combat identity; deepen decisions rather than adding a tactical grid.

tasks.title: Economy, supplies and expedition pressure balance
tasks.goal: Make gold, rations, rest, shops and expedition resources create sustained but fair pressure across the 18-day campaign.
acceptance_criteria: Audit income, prices, ration use, rest costs and common resource drains across representative runs.
Reduce trivial infinite-value or obviously bad-value transactions and resource loops.
Make settlement services and purchases create real trade-offs without requiring grind.
Ensure poor early luck does not routinely create an unrecoverable campaign spiral.
Document target balance assumptions so later content can price rewards consistently.
tasks.notes: Mechanist owns base prices, income, costs and resource-pressure balance. Consume LR-0005 faction modifier hooks rather than duplicating consequence logic.

tasks.title: Equipment ecosystem and meaningful itemisation
tasks.goal: Expand LR-0006's equipment/build foundation into a small but expressive item ecosystem with meaningful trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Equipment categories/slots from the progression foundation are used consistently.
Add a curated set of distinct equipment choices rather than straight numerical upgrades.
Items support different hero/build identities and situational strategies.
Rare or powerful items have opportunity costs, constraints or meaningful competition.
Shop, reward and save/load flows correctly support the expanded equipment data.

Economy boundary: LR-0017 owns item categories, effects, availability and equip/reward plumbing; LR-0016 owns global base prices/income/resource-pressure targets, with LR-0020 providing final whole-system tuning.

acceptance_criteria: Define a compact set of distinct injuries/conditions with mechanical and narrative-facing effects.
Conditions can arise from understandable risks rather than arbitrary punishment.
Recovery has meaningful costs, choices or time pressure instead of a single automatic reset.
Party members remain viable; injuries create stories and adaptation rather than routine run-ending snowballs.
Persistence and migration behave correctly through save/load.

Economy boundary: recovery costs and resource drains must consume the target assumptions established by LR-0016; LR-0018 owns injury/recovery mechanics, not global economy rebalance.

tasks.title: Encounter variety, elites and signature fights

acceptance_criteria: Create encounter compositions that demand different tactical responses.
Add a small number of elite/signature enemies or fight modifiers with recognisable identities.
Major encounters can use bespoke rules or phases where justified without creating one-off engine fragility.
Difficulty escalation is readable and appropriate to campaign timing.
Encounter rewards and risks remain consistent with economy/progression expectations.
tasks.notes: Blocked on LR-0015 because encounter design should exploit the finished combat-depth vocabulary. Economy boundary: encounter reward/risk values must use LR-0016's documented economy assumptions; this task owns encounter composition/signature mechanics, not global price or income tuning.

tasks.title: Build viability and whole-system balance pass
tasks.goal: Balance the completed Mechanist systems as one coherent game so multiple strategies remain viable across a full campaign.
acceptance_criteria: Test representative campaigns using materially different hero builds and spending strategies.
Identify and correct dominant, trap and non-functional choices.
Check difficulty, resource pressure and progression pacing across early, mid and late campaign.
Ensure combat rewards, equipment, recovery costs and economy reinforce rather than undermine each other.
Record remaining balance uncertainties and create targeted follow-up tasks instead of endless unscoped tweaking.
tasks.notes: Mechanist capstone task. Blocked until its underlying systems exist.

tasks.title: Baseline full-campaign black-box playtest
tasks.goal: Play Lantern Road as a normal player from a fresh campaign through as much of the 18-day arc as possible and identify the highest-impact failures in fun, clarity, pacing and reliability.
acceptance_criteria: Start from a fresh campaign without relying on internal implementation knowledge.
Record major player decisions, progression, friction points and any point where the next action is unclear.
Capture reproducible bugs, soft-locks, broken states, pacing problems, boring/repetitive stretches and moments that feel especially strong.
Classify findings by severity and player impact.
Check the existing queue before creating non-duplicate follow-up tasks and assign each new finding to the appropriate specialist agent.
tasks.notes: The single intentional early QA pass. Establish a baseline before the foundations change; findings may become stale and must be retested later. Real-browser execution is required.

tasks.title: Every-action and navigation black-box audit
tasks.goal: Systematically exercise every visible player control and navigation path to find inert, misleading, inconsistent or unintuitive interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise top-bar controls, map interactions, tabs, settlement/site actions, dialogue choices, shops, camp, combat and save/load controls.
Identify controls that appear to do nothing, give insufficient feedback, have unclear labels, or produce surprising results.
Record reproducible steps and expected versus observed player-facing behaviour.
Test both successful actions and blocked/no-op states.
Route non-duplicate findings to the appropriate specialist rather than implementing fixes directly.
tasks.notes: QA counterpart to LR-0001/LR-0009; evaluates player experience rather than implementing UI changes. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Save, load and resume destructive playtest
tasks.goal: Try to break campaign persistence through real player save/load/resume behaviour and unusual timing/state combinations.
acceptance_criteria: Save and reload from settlements, travel, sites, dialogue/event states and combat where supported.
Test repeated loads, refreshing/reopening the browser, partial progress and unusual action sequences.
Look for duplicated rewards, lost progress, impossible states, stale UI and corrupted or inconsistent restored state.
Record exact reproduction paths and whether the failure is deterministic.
Create non-duplicate findings for The Steward or relevant specialist; do not repair save internals within the QA task.
tasks.notes: A later release-candidate regression retests persistence after save hardening and feature integration. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Exploit, resource-loop and soft-lock hunt
tasks.goal: Actively attempt to abuse Lantern Road's systems to find infinite resources, repeatable rewards, sequence breaks, unwinnable states and other player-visible exploits.
acceptance_criteria: Try repeated site actions, rest/shop loops, travel/camp loops, save/load abuse and reward re-entry.
Look for infinite gold/rations/items/renown, free healing, repeatable quest rewards and bypassed costs.
Identify soft-locks or states where the campaign remains technically running but meaningful progress is impossible.
Rate exploit severity based on ease, impact and likelihood of accidental discovery.
Route each reproducible non-duplicate finding to the appropriate specialist.
tasks.notes: Deliberately adversarial player testing. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA. Dependency audit: run after equipment, injury/recovery and signature-encounter systems exist so item/healing/reward re-entry exploits are not tested against an incomplete economy surface.

tasks.title: Quest-path and impossible-state audit
tasks.goal: Test quest and site progression for dead ends, contradictory state, unavailable required actions and sequence-sensitive failures.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise different ordering of rumours, quest acceptance, travel, site resolution and faction-facing decisions.
Look for objectives that cannot be completed, completed objectives that remain active, unavailable required NPC/site actions and contradictory journal/state text.
Test revisiting resolved and partially resolved locations.
Record the smallest reproducible state/path for each failure.
Create non-duplicate specialist tasks rather than rewriting quest code directly.
tasks.notes: Focus is state integrity and player completion paths, not authorship. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Fresh-player clarity and onboarding playtest
tasks.goal: Approach Lantern Road as if seeing it for the first time and identify where the game fails to teach goals, controls, terminology, consequences or next steps naturally.
acceptance_criteria: Begin without consulting README/internal documentation.
Record every point where the player's goal, available action, cost, risk or expected outcome is unclear.
Assess information density, jargon, tutorialisation-by-play and whether important systems surface at the right time.
Distinguish genuine confusion from intentional uncertainty or mystery.
Route recommendations to the appropriate specialist without turning the QA task into a redesign implementation.
tasks.notes: Tests intuitiveness rather than raw functionality. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Narrative continuity and consequence playtest
tasks.goal: Play branching narrative paths after the Storyteller foundation is complete and find dialogue, memory, consequence and ending contradictions.
acceptance_criteria: Test materially different decisions and faction alignments.
Look for characters forgetting major events, inappropriate dialogue, contradictory relationship reactions and consequences that fail to surface.
Verify endings acknowledge relevant named decisions and campaign outcomes.
Assess whether consequences feel understandable rather than merely hidden state changes.
Route reproducible findings to The Storyteller or Steward as appropriate.
tasks.notes: Unlocks after the first narrative/consequence/event/campaign wave. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Combat fun, difficulty and tedium playtest
tasks.goal: Evaluate whether the deeper combat system is readable, varied, fair and enjoyable across repeated encounters rather than merely mechanically functional.
acceptance_criteria: Play multiple encounter types using different party/build approaches.
Identify dominant actions, fake choices, difficulty spikes, trivial fights, excessive repetition and unclear enemy behaviour.
Assess perceived battle length and decision density rather than only win/loss outcomes.
Test whether signature/elite encounters actually require different thinking.
Route balance/design findings to The Mechanist with reproducible examples.
tasks.notes: Player-experience validation of Mechanist combat work. Real-browser execution is required; code inspection alone is not black-box QA.

tasks.title: Phone one-handed usability black-box playtest

acceptance_criteria: Play substantial sessions in portrait orientation using touch only.
Test map tap/pan/zoom, modals, choice cards, combat, scrolling, text sizing and save/resume flows.
Look for accidental taps, obscured controls, reachability problems, tiny targets and excessive scrolling.
Assess one-handed comfort and whether feedback is visible without hunting through logs.
Route findings to The Wayfinder or relevant specialist.

agent_roster.name: The Steward
agent_roster.role: Lead, architecture, integration, production discipline, cross-system consistency, bug triage and code review.

agent_roster.name: The Storyteller
agent_roster.role: Narrative, characters, dialogue, quests, consequences, campaign structure and endings.

agent_roster.name: The Mechanist
agent_roster.role: Combat, equipment, abilities, injuries, builds, economy, balance and deeper gameplay systems.

agent_roster.name: The Lamplighter
agent_roster.role: Art direction, UI feedback, animation, map presentation, sound, ambience and overall feel.

agent_roster.name: The Wayfinder
agent_roster.role: Mobile UX, accessibility, save/autosave usability, touch/map behaviour, testing, edge cases and interaction audits.

agent_roster.name: The Warden
agent_roster.role: QA, black-box playtesting and player experience. Repeatedly plays Lantern Road, tries to break it, identifies bugs, exploits, confusion, tedium, pacing and fun problems, and routes reproducible findings back to the appropriate specialist rather than implementing feature fixes.

agent_roster.name: The Director
agent_roster.role: Design direction and production governance. Owns the product vision, terminology and decision log; reviews feature work for pillar alignment, tone/coherence, scope drift and cross-task conflicts; does not replace Josh as final creative director.

foundation_gates.rationale: The ideal architecture/save/test foundations were identified after the first specialist wave had already been claimed. Do not invalidate live work mid-branch. Finish the listed in-flight wave under merge gates, then complete modularisation before new feature work.
